title.narrative: Health vouchers at YRCS Hajjah facility/ GRC

description.narrative:
After several years of supporting the YRCS Hajjah clinic in Yemen through contributions to the GRC, we are now shifting our support to GRC to implement an initiative providing health vouchers to cover health-related costs at the facility. The idea is to offer cash assistance through health vouchers to vulnerable families, enabling them to cover health-related expenses at the Hajjah health facility. This initiative would ensure these families can access essential healthcare while supporting the facility's operational costs, allowing it to run independently. It would also strengthen GRC's Mother and Child Health portfolio and provide valuable insights into integrating cash assistance into health programming, with potential for future expansion. Moreover, this aligns with BRC's PIAs. Potential Target Group:
Internally Displaced Persons in Hajjah, particularly pregnant women, mothers, and children who are unable to afford the required health service fees. Vulnerable individuals within the host communities, especially pregnant women, mothers, and children, who are also unable to afford health service fees. Selection criteria will be defined during the proposal stage.
Key Needs:
Health Services: Access to primary and specialized care, particularly for those with chronic or emergency health conditions. Transport: Financial assistance for transportation to the health facility, especially for those living at a distance. Cash Support: GRC aims to provide health vouchers to approximately 600 households, with an estimated transfer of 200 USD per household. This translates to approximately 120,000 USD for transfers, 25,000 USD for assessments, service provider fees, post-distribution monitoring (PDM), and lessons learned, and 25,000 USD for staff costs. The total estimated budget is approximately 170,000 USD. This is a preliminary estimate, which will be refined during the proposal stage.
This funding would help ensure that families can access necessary healthcare without incurring debt or forgoing critical treatments.
